dialogues.text: Yes. I probably won't be coming back. I've decided to leave this place.
All right. How much are you applying for?
If you've decided to leave, why keep helping others?
One last time. And I wanted to say goodbye while I was here.
I hope you find a fresh start.
(Hands over the documents) This will be the last time we see each other. Let's just go through the formalities.

final_dialogues.text: You seem quieter than usual today.
Do I?
You do. When I came before, you'd always ask, 'Who is it this time?'
Because you always had a new reason.
Yeah.
Are you really leaving for good? Have you truly decided this time?
Yeah. This time, I really am leaving.
You've said things like that before.
Before, I always had a clear goal.
And now you don't?
Whenever I helped each of them, I thought they were only short of a little time.
I wanted to fill that gap with my own, as much as I could. I thought it would make their lives better.
Ryan was just short of enough time to step into a new life. Mike was just short of enough time to support his family. Mary was just short of enough time to stay alive.
Sometimes I even thought Lisa was only short of enough time to overturn this company's system. If I were stronger, if I could rise high enough...
Could I overturn the company's decision? Could I make it so no one had to work overtime anymore?
But you did help them. Ryan, Mike, and Mary's lives have improved.
But what was the outcome?
I used to think this world simply needed more people willing to lend a hand.
Later, I realized it might not be that no one reaches out.
Under a system like this, everyone is stuck in the mire.
So you won't help anyone anymore?
I don't know.
But for now, I've decided to leave.
My parents told me they do not have much time left either. I want to go back and see them.
I wish you all the best, Brooks.
